results.trace: Read src/ui/race-ui.ts:95 and :122-126 and src/ui/best-laps.ts. The stored best is read once in reset() and compared against that snapshot. That matches the spec: 'the HUD BEST chip shows the lower of stored and this race's laps', and AC1/AC3/AC7 all put the stored value in place before the race starts.
results.reason: This only happens if another tab writes the same key while a race is running. That is outside the spec, which defines the stored best as what is in storage when the race starts. Re-reading storage on every lap would be new behaviour, not a fix for anything the spec requires.

results.trace: Read race-ui.ts:20-23 and :78-84 (newBestPhase returns 'out' for since < NEW_BEST_BACK_TICKS, 'back' until NEW_BEST_GONE_TICKS, then null) and hud.ts:154-159. The phase is 'out' from lapEnd to lapEnd+STILL_OUT, so a test asserting class is-out in that window would pass on this branch.
results.reason: This is a missing test, not a bug: the branch code shows the chip correctly during the slide-out window. No test can fail on this branch because of it, so there is nothing to fix.

results.trace: hud.ts:157-158 toggle is-out/is-back. hud.css:152-159 makes the chip visible and slid down under .is-out, and visible under .is-back. The classes are set as the spec requires.
results.reason: This only describes a mutation the tests wouldn't catch. The shipped code toggles the classes correctly, so no failing test is possible and there is no defect to fix.

results.trace: race-ui.ts:95 reads only when info.trackId is defined, and the write and newBestTick assignment sit inside `if (race.trackId !== undefined)`. So without a track id nothing is read or saved and no chip is shown, as the spec requires.
results.reason: The guard behaves as the spec says. The finding only points out a coverage gap under a hypothetical mutation, with no bug on this branch.
